validation_gates.reason: _time accepted only a trailing uppercase 'Z' and returned None for every other RFC 3339 form the schema's date-time format accepts (+00:00, -05:00, lowercase 't'/'z'). An unreadable revoked_at was then treated as absent, so a ReviewPacketReference revoked at 2026-04-13T06:00:00+00:00 and evaluated at 12:00Z passed with status ACTIVE (fail-open), while the same instant written with Z was correctly rejected. The same parser wrongly rejected valid packet and time-slice timestamps in any other offset. _time now parses every RFC 3339 offset and normalizes to UTC, and a present but unreadable revoked_at fails as REVIEW_PACKET_TIME_INVALID. A valid instant that overflows when normalized to UTC, such as 0001-01-01T00:00:00+00:01, is a time-invalid finding rather than an OverflowError (review finding on #5298). The reader also reported deeply nested JSON and over-long integers as tracebacks and accepted NaN; these now report JSON_INVALID or JSON_NONFINITE_NUMBER. Six of the new tests fail on the original code.

tests/release/test_trust_projection_manifest.py: 14 tests (4 before, 10 new) covering UTC-range overflow, revocation in every offset including the inclusive boundary, offset-agnostic packet and time-slice intervals, the unreadable-revocation rule, packet lifecycle (not yet issued, zero-length validity, inclusive expiry), time-slice duplicates and correction requirements, asset-integrity outcome derivation, the governance decision requirement, every reader finding and the CLI. Branch coverage of the validator rises from 61% to 89%.

Each of nineteen changes failed the suite, among them removing case normalization, the UTC-overflow handling, the offset requirement, UTC normalization, the unreadable-revocation rule, the inclusive revocation and expiry boundaries, the not-yet-issued rule, the finite-float hook and check, the broadened JSON exception, each time-slice and asset rule, the decision-requirement event set and the CLI exit code.
